title: [P1][inventory,data-integrity] "Used some" fraction actions: inconsistent confirm step and silent no-op at zero stock
goal: Two compounding gaps in the same file cluster: (1) the 25/50/75% quick-fraction buttons in consume-actions.tsx:74-80 write a ledger movement on a single tap with no ConfirmPanel step, inconsistent with 'Used it up'/'Wasted' which require one via S-69's shared pattern; (2) requestedAmount = fraction * item.virtualStockBase in lib/inventory/consume.ts:26-43 resolves to 0 whenever virtualStockBase is already 0, and recordConsumption returns early with no write and no error -- the user taps 25%, the confirm panel closes (once added per this story), and nothing visibly changes with no explanation that there was nothing to log against the displayed stock.
in_scope: Route the 25/50/75% fraction buttons through the same ConfirmPanel step already used for 'Used it up'/'Wasted' in consume-actions.tsx.
recordConsumption (lib/inventory/consume.ts): when virtualStockBase is already 0, surface an explicit 'nothing to log' message instead of silently returning {ok: true} with no write.
out_of_scope: Changing the fraction calculation itself or virtualStockBase's underlying formula -- REQ-14 scope, not this story.
Touch-target sizing on these same buttons -- covered separately by S-95.
acceptance: The 25/50/75% quick-fraction buttons require the same confirm step as 'Used it up'/'Wasted' before writing a ledger movement. Tapping a fraction action when virtualStockBase is already 0 surfaces an explicit 'nothing to log' message instead of silently no-op'ing with {ok: true} and no visible change.
invariants: The confirm-step addition must not regress the manual-amount 'Used some' path, which the code comment says already requires typing an amount plus a separate Log click -- that path's existing friction level should stay as-is; this story fixes the fraction shortcuts specifically.
